suppliers.required_interface: UQ1 supplies the finite product-law PCE setup, the degree-one orthonormal polynomial family under a positive moment Gram matrix, and the finite tensor-basis construction. No finite cutoff or moment assumption supplies general completeness; UQ2 states completeness separately and proves it directly in the four-point example.

supplier_excerpts.quote: It is only a finite-degree condition; it does not assert that polynomials are dense in any $L^2(\rho_j)$.

Applying the finite Gram–Schmidt recursion to this ordered list gives real orthonormal polynomials $\phi_{j,0},\ldots,\phi_{j,p_j}$, where $\phi_{j,k}$ has degree $k$, positive leading coefficient, and $\phi_{j,0}=1$.

Let $\phi_{j,k}$ be the Gram–Schmidt polynomials from
[[lem-positive-moment-gram-produces-univariate-chaos-polynomials]], and let
$\Lambda$ be a finite subset of the admissible degree box in
[[def-finite-product-chaos-input]].

suppliers.required_interface: For independent symmetric two-point marginals and cutoff one, finite product input data has product law, the degree-one Gram matrix is positive definite and Gram–Schmidt gives modes 1 and x; the tensor-basis definition forms products over the declared finite index set. The consumer proves this particular four-mode family is orthonormal and complete on the four-point support, so it assumes no global PCE completeness.

supplier_excerpts.quote: It is only a finite-degree condition; it does not assert that polynomials are dense in any $L^2(\rho_j)$.

Applying the finite Gram–Schmidt recursion to this ordered list gives real orthonormal polynomials $\phi_{j,0},\ldots,\phi_{j,p_j}$, where $\phi_{j,k}$ has degree $k$, positive leading coefficient, and $\phi_{j,0}=1$.

Let $\phi_{j,k}$ be the Gram–Schmidt polynomials from
[[lem-positive-moment-gram-produces-univariate-chaos-polynomials]], and let
$\Lambda$ be a finite subset of the admissible degree box in

$$\psi_\alpha(y_1,\ldots,y_d)=\prod_{j=1}^d\phi_{j,\alpha_j}(y_j).$$
